blogs.title: When a “Huge Adnexal Mass” Is Actually a Fibroid: Diagnostic Traps in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post would explore how uterine leiomyomas can masquerade as adnexal cystic masses in pregnancy, especially when they are pedunculated, degenerating, posterior, or displaced by the gravid uterus. It would review bedside clues from bimanual exam, ultrasound, Doppler, and non-contrast MRI, and discuss why an apparently ovarian lesion may still be uterine in origin.

blogs.title: CA-125 in the Second Trimester: Signal, Noise, or Red Herring?
blogs.description: This post would examine the limited utility of tumor markers during pregnancy, using this case’s mildly rising CA-125 as a teaching point. It would discuss normal pregnancy-related variation, the poor specificity of isolated elevations, and how clinicians should integrate marker trends with imaging and clinical status rather than letting a borderline abnormal value drive overly aggressive management.

blogs.title: Operate or Observe? The Management Tension of Symptomatic Pelvic Masses in Pregnancy
blogs.description: This post would focus on the central decision in the case: conservative management versus surgery for a large symptomatic abdominal mass in the second trimester. It would analyze the indications that push clinicians toward intervention—pain, dyspnea, uncertain diagnosis, torsion, rupture, infection, and space-occupying effects—while contrasting them with the obstetric risks of laparotomy and myomectomy.

blogs.title: Pregnant, Dyspneic, and Full of Fibroids: Mass Effect as a Real Maternal Complication
blogs.description: This post would highlight an underappreciated issue in obstetric medicine: restrictive symptoms from massive intra-abdominal lesions. Using this patient’s dyspnea and pain, it would discuss how clinicians should evaluate mechanical respiratory compromise in pregnancy, distinguish it from cardiopulmonary disease, and recognize when mass effect itself becomes a legitimate indication for procedural intervention.

blogs.title: Myomectomy During Pregnancy: How to Do Less, Safely
blogs.description: This post would use the operation itself to teach surgical restraint in pregnancy. It would cover the rationale for removing only the torsed, leaking pedunculated fibroid while leaving the fixed pelvic mass in situ, principles of minimizing uterine manipulation and bleeding, intraoperative fetal assessment, and why the safest pregnancy-preserving surgery is often the shortest and most targeted one.

blogs.title: The Fibroid That Determines the Delivery: Planning Birth Around Residual Pelvic Obstruction
blogs.description: This post would examine how fibroid size, number, and location influence mode of delivery. It would discuss why the residual caudal myoma represented a likely mechanical barrier to labor, how postpartum fibroid regression factors into timing of definitive treatment, and how clinicians can individualize cesarean planning in patients with persistent lower uterine segment or pelvic masses.
